outcome: positive birth experience (overall score and domains: professional support, perceived safety, own capacity)
cohort: The study included 301 women who experienced childbirth in Spain, recruited via consecutive sampling.
finding: Key predictors of lower positive birth experience scores included higher maternal education, increased intrapartum interventions, inductions of labour, instrumental deliveries, caesarean births, epidural analgesia, and NICU admission, while having a midwife and higher neonatal Apgar scores predicted better experiences.
mod_finding: Caesarean births and instrumental deliveries were inversely related to a positive overall birth experience, perceived safety, and own capacity, whereas spontaneous labour onset predicted better capacity and safety.
